paragraphs: Clerical dress is one of the few costumes still worn daily that has not changed in living memory, and it is legible instantly: black, a collar, and a book held rather than carried. The book is what turns a standing figure into someone in the middle of a duty.
The character is light at 13,968 polygons and 13,663 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, suited to background and crowd use, and carries StemCell certification.

At $99 it suits architectural and interior visualisation, historical and religious scenes, education and documentary work, film previsualisation, game crowds and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

An underground lake is the quietest place most people will ever stand in. Still water in complete darkness, formed where the rock is soluble and the water table sits above the floor, and every reflection in it is perfect because nothing up there moves the surface.
This is supplied as a scene rather than a single object, and it carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $99 it suits game environments, film and television, documentary and education work, fantasy and adventure illustration, and architectural visualisation of natural spaces. On sale since 2023.

Centre pivot irrigation is why so much farmland seen from the air is circular. A single arm on wheels walks slowly around a well at the middle of the field, and everything outside the circle it can reach stays dry. The landscape was redrawn to fit the machine.
The model holds 570,770 polygons and 600,135 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 9 maps all at 4096x4096. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $99 it suits agricultural and agritech visualisation, equipment marketing, environmental and water use presentation, documentary work, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2018.

A burrowing crab spends most of its life below the sand and only appears when the tide is right. The asymmetry is the giveaway: one claw much larger than the other, used for display and defence rather than for feeding.
The model is very light at 7,986 polygons and 8,075 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, so several can populate a shoreline at once. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $99 it suits coastal and marine visualisation, nature documentary and education work, game environments, advertising and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

The Colossi have stood in a field outside Luxor for thirty four centuries, guarding a mortuary temple that no longer exists behind them. One of them was famous in antiquity for singing at dawn, a sound produced by cracked stone and stopped forever by a Roman repair.
The model is light at 20,158 polygons and 20,459 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, suited to wide scenes and background use. It is built to CheckMate specification.

At $99 it suits historical and archaeological visualisation, museum and exhibition work, documentary and education material, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

A straddle carrier picks a container up by standing over it, which is why the machine looks like a building on stilts. It moves boxes around a terminal faster than a crane can hand them over, and it can stack them without any other equipment involved.

The model holds 243,257 polygons and 258,033 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 14 maps all at 4096x4096, in clean condition. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $99 it suits port and logistics visualisation, equipment marketing, infrastructure presentation, documentary work, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2020.

Bike share machines are built to be abused: heavy frames, internal gears, puncture resistant tyres, and no component worth stealing. They are deliberately slow and deliberately ugly, and they work precisely because nobody wants to take one home.

The model holds 148,983 polygons and 151,432 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured generously with 61 maps, 60 at 4096x4096 and one at 2048x2048. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a generic bike share build is offered separately.
At $99 it suits urban and architectural visualisation, transport and mobility presentation, advertising, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2016.

A luxury sports watch is a contradiction the industry took decades to accept: a case built for water and knocks, finished to a standard that assumes it will never see either. The embossed strap and the rounded octagonal case are what make this family recognisable across a room.
The model holds 85,480 polygons and 92,798 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in black, which is enough resolution for close product renders. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $99 it suits product and jewellery visualisation, e-commerce and catalogue imagery, advertising, editorial illustration and film props. On sale since 2025.

An indoor court is a room with very specific dimensions and almost nothing in it. The run off behind the baseline, the height above the net and the colour of the walls are all regulated, because a player has to be able to see a ball moving at speed against them.
The scene holds 498,021 polygons and 534,358 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in wood and red, with the net and post covers included. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $99 it suits sports facility visualisation, architectural and interior presentation, equipment and club marketing, broadcast graphics, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2025.

A mole is a digging machine with fur on it. The forelimbs are rotated so the palms face outward permanently, the eyes are all but useless, and the fur has no grain so the animal can reverse down a tunnel without it catching.

The model holds 24,931 polygons and 18,147 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and comes rigged for posing or animation. It is built to CheckMate specification, and native rigged builds for Maya and Cinema 4D are offered separately.
At $99 it suits wildlife and nature visualisation, education and documentary work, garden and pest control presentation, animation, game creatures and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.

Scrubs became a fashion category surprisingly recently. The cut, the fabric and the colour used to be dictated by the hospital laundry, and now they are chosen by the person wearing them, usually with a pair of cushioned trainers that were designed for running.
The outfit holds 48,283 polygons and 50,149 vertices in quads and tris with overlapping UVs, in purple and black with the footwear included. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $99 it suits apparel and retail visualisation, healthcare uniform marketing, e-commerce imagery, advertising, character work and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.

Science fiction weapon design mostly consists of deciding what to keep. A shotgun is recognisable by its pump, its bore and the way it is held, so a futuristic one has to preserve at least one of those or the audience will not know what they are looking at.
This is a collection listing rather than a single object, supplying the weapons as static pieces. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $99 the set suits game weapons and characters, science fiction film and animation, concept art, previsualisation and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.

A salon is a workshop that has to look like a lounge. Every chair, basin and dryer is a piece of equipment with plumbing or power behind it, styled so the client never thinks about that, and the arrangement of them is what makes the room work.

This is a collection listing rather than a single object, supplying the equipment as static pieces. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and two further volumes of the set are offered separately.
At $99 it suits interior and architectural visualisation, salon and retail presentation, equipment marketing, advertising, film sets and game environments. On sale since 2019.

Flying high is a design problem before it is a tactical one. The wing has to be enormous relative to the fuselage because the air is thin, the engines have to work where there is almost nothing to breathe, and the resulting aircraft handles like a glider that happens to have jets.
The airframe holds 187,404 polygons and 102,834 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in grey, and carries StemCell certification for use across engines and renderers.
At $99 it suits defence and aviation visualisation, documentary and news graphics, flight simulation, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2023.
